Rules / Maintainability

SK7003 The member is over the statement-count threshold

Method length counted in statements, not in lines.

CategoryMaintainability
Default severityhint
ScopeSyntax
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseyes
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since0.8

Why

Counting lines makes the metric a function of the formatter: the same body scores differently at a 100-column width and at a 160-column one, and wrapping a long argument list makes a method "longer" without changing anything a reader has to understand. Counting statements is invariant under formatting, which is the property that makes the number worth putting in a gate at all. Declarations, expression statements, and each statement nested inside a block are counted once each; a for header is one statement, not three.

Example

Instead of:

// a 300-statement method

Write:

// the same work as several members with names

When it does not fire

A metric rule has no false positives in the sense doc 16 § R3 means: it reports a measurement against a threshold, and the measurement is either right or a bug. What it can be is useless — a threshold low enough to fire on ordinary code teaches people to switch the category off, which is the same outcome by another route. The default is therefore set well above the corpus's p99 rather than at the textbook number, and the threshold is an .editorconfig option so a repository can tighten it deliberately. Generated code is excluded from the rule entirely; doc 07 § Metrics keeps it in the aggregate numbers, which is a separate surface.

Configuration

  • dotnet_diagnostic.SK7003.severity
  • dotnet_code_quality.SK7003.threshold (default 120)
